svg.title: Reset and memory wake-up
svg.desc: From reset to the first instruction: the chip wakes its own flash and RAMs, in six steps that work whatever state the chips were left in. Recorded from an RTL simulation, not computed in the browser. Made by docs/tools/motion.py from docs/site/data/traces/reset.json.

text.tspan: From reset to the first instruction: the chip wakes its own flash and RAMs, in six steps that work whatever state the
Reset held: rst_n is low, every uio pin is an input (uio_oe = 0x00), so the demo board could program the flash now.
ui_in[2:0] are being latched as the QSPI read latency (0 here).
Reset released. qspi_ctrl starts its wake-up sequence before the core may fetch anything: neither memory understands
four-bit transactions yet. Step 1 of 6 starts at once: flash: all four lines high, 8 clocks (leave continuous read).
Wake-up step 2 of 6, flash: command 0xEB, one bit per clock (Fast Read Quad I/O).
Wake-up step 3 of 6, flash: address 0 and mode 0xA0, four bits per clock (stay in continuous read).
Wake-up step 4 of 6, flash: 4 dummy clocks and one byte, then chip select high.
Wake-up step 5 of 6, both RAMs: 0xF5, four bits per clock (leave QPI if a previous run left it on).
Wake-up step 6 of 6, both RAMs: 0x35, one bit per clock (enter QPI).
Both memories awake: the testbench counts 99 clocks from reset release (1.98 us at 50 MHz). The flash is in continuous
read and the RAMs in QPI mode; the core's first fetch goes out.
Cycle 138: the first instruction word arrives (imem_rvalid). The program starts at flash address 0.
